requirement:
`OutlineContent::language()` returns the name of the `OutlineLang` that produced
the snapshot. The root and each selected item report the same name. An explicit
provider supplies its own name, including when the filename would select a
different language by default.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.language` that needs implementation evidence, so no implementation roots are needed. Every clause specifies observable behavior:

- "`OutlineContent::language()` returns the name of the `OutlineLang` that produced the snapshot." This is a value the method returns. Reading the name from a snapshot field, as `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineContent]/fn[language]` does, or looking it up some other way would give the same results. The method's signature, `pub fn language(&self) -> &str`, is declared in the sibling outline-contents declaration in `md/requirements/sdk/outlines.md`, not in this requirement.
- "The root and each selected item report the same name." This is an output property. Any implementation with one language name per snapshot satisfies it.
- "An explicit provider supplies its own name, including when the filename would select a different language by default." This is a precedence rule about observable results. It names no library, algorithm, type, field or delegation interface.

I could find no alternative implementation that keeps these behaviors and still violates a clause. Tests can cover the behavior.

behavioral: The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.language`.

- **Root reports the producing language's name.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[default_language_names_match_the_retained_outline]` builds roots with `OutlineContent::from_source` for `LIB.RS`, `widget.TSX`, `README` and `foo.unknown`. It asserts that `root.language()` equals `rust`, `tsx`, `plain-text` and `plain-text`. It also checks that each name equals `languages::name_for_path`.
- **Explicit provider supplies its own name, even when the filename would select another language.** `fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` uses a `CustomLanguage` named `custom` with the misleading filename `misleading.rs`, which would default to rust. It builds a root through both `from_source_with` and `from_path_with`. In both cases it asserts `root.language() == "custom"`.
- **Selected item reports the same name as the root.** The same test calls `select("part[selected]")` on the supplied root and asserts `selected.language() == "custom"`. It makes this check after dropping the language object, so the name must come from the retained snapshot.

The selected-item check runs only for the explicit provider, not for the default languages. The implementation stores `language` in the shared `Snapshot` and returns `&self.snapshot.language`, so selection has no separate branch for the name. I treated this as the same input class and not a gap.
